title: Ordinary locally finite-free sheaf evaluation and biduality
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site small in the coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention], $R$ any sheaf of commutative rings, and $M$ an $R$-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Suppose there is a small family of objects $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ such that, for every $V\in\mathcal C$, the sieve of arrows $W\to V$ with $W$ admitting a morphism to some $U_i$ is covering. Suppose that on each slice $\mathcal C/U_i$ there is an isomorphism $M|_{U_i}\cong(R|_{U_i})^{\oplus r_i}$ with $r_i\geq0$ finite, allowed to vary with $i$. Write $D_R(M)=\mathcal Hom_R(M,R)$ using the slice-Hom of [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. There is a natural module-sheaf map
$$\delta_M:M\longrightarrow D_R^2(M),\qquad \delta_M(x)_V(\lambda)=\lambda(x|_V)$$
for every $x\in M(U)$, $V\to U$, and local functional $\lambda$. Formation of $D_R$, $D_R^2$ and $\delta_M$ commutes with restriction to any slice, with coefficients restricted to that slice. For every module map $f:M\to N$, $D_R^2(f)\delta_M=\delta_N f$ (the same evaluation map for arbitrary $N$).

The dual $D_R(M)$ is finite free of rank $r_i$ on the same slices, and $\delta_M$ is an isomorphism of $R$-module sheaves. More precisely, for each chosen local basis $e_1,\ldots,e_{r_i}$, let $e_j^*$ be the coordinate functionals. On every further slice the dual-basis coordinate isomorphism sends $\lambda$ to $(\lambda(e_j))_j$, and the restriction of $\delta_M^{-1}$ is
$$\eta\longmapsto\sum_{j=1}^{r_i}\eta(e_j^*)e_j.$$
These formulas are compatible with further restriction, including the empty sum at rank zero. No global rank bound, points of the site, or global finite-free retract of $M$ is required.

Identity restrictions and restrictOver_hom_app_congr identify the slice components. Finite sums include rank zero without a separate assumption.
